title: Finite-sum bilevel optimization with strong convexity only in the average lower level.
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the stated error criterion and guarantee. Assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately. Here $f=n_f^{-1}\sum_i f_i$ and $g=n_g^{-1}\sum_jg_j$.

description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the stated error criterion and guarantee. Assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately. Here $f=n_f^{-1}\sum_i f_i$ and $g=n_g^{-1}\sum_jg_j$.

model.lower_geometry: The average g(x,·) is μ_y-strongly convex. Individual g_j may be nonconvex.
regularity: Every $\nabla f_i$ and $\nabla g_j$ is jointly $L$-Lipschitz.
The xy and yy blocks of every g_j are jointly rho-Lipschitz.
The bound ‖∇_y f‖ ≤ B_f is imposed only on the average f.
model.bounded_below: Phi is finite and bounded below; its public initial gap is at most Delta.
description_paragraphs: Each component gradient is $L$-Lipschitz in the joint Euclidean space. The $xy,yy$ Hessian block of every $g_j$ is $\rho$-Lipschitz. Only the average $g(x,\cdot)$ must be $\mu_y$-strongly convex; individual $g_j$ may be nonconvex.
Only the average upper-level function must satisfy $\|\nabla_yf\|\le B_f$. The function $\Phi$ is bounded below, and $\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$ and $\|y_0-y^*(x_0)\|\le R_y$ hold.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: The algorithm selects (i,x,y) and receives exact ∇f_i.
A query $(j,x,y)$ returns the exact gradient $\nabla g_j$.
oracle.coupling: Any component may be revisited; each access is charged.
oracle.query_domain: The full space, with component indices publicly selectable.
description_paragraphs: Component counts, dimensions, budgets, and initial points are public. The algorithm chooses $(i,x,y)$ to obtain exact $\nabla f_i(x,y)$, or chooses $(j,x,y)$ to obtain exact $\nabla g_j(x,y)$. Any component may be queried repeatedly throughout the full space. There is no sample noise or additional hidden-solution interface.
Return any measurable $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$; unqueried outputs are allowed, with no inner point or certificate required.
The resource is $N=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}$, with one unit per full component gradient. A complete scan costs $n_f+n_g$. The budget is fixed on every execution path.

Arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms are allowed, with measurable queries, stopping, and postprocessing. Outputs may be unqueried, randomly selected historical points, or admissible averages. No span or zero-respecting restriction applies. Queries are sequential; each response in a batch is charged. Internal arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage are free, with no separate work, memory, or communication budget.
For each instance, require $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2\le\varepsilon^2$. Expectation is over algorithmic randomness only.

notes: The source lower bound covers randomized adaptive algorithms with arbitrary measurable outputs, using selectable exact full component gradients at both levels and a fixed worst-case budget.

Each lower component is strongly convex in all three hard families, so the lower population average is strongly convex as required here. The lower Hessians are constant and satisfy the target block regularity.
Choose the public starting points to be zero. The lower optimum at the starting point is zero in the amplified-chain and upper-needle families, and at distance one in the lower-needle family.
The componentwise strongly convex upper bound in the source has a stronger assumption than this profile. A matching upper bound for this profile remains unrecorded.
